snippet.title: The Wow! Signal: 72 Seconds That Never Came Back
snippet.description:
On August 15, 1977, Ohio's Big Ear radio telescope recorded a 72-second narrowband burst so striking that astronomer Jerry Ehman circled the printout and wrote one word: Wow!

This documentary reconstructs what the instrument was listening for, why the hydrogen line mattered to SETI, what made the event look non-ordinary, and why decades of follow-up still failed to catch a second pulse.

What you'll learn:
- How Big Ear surveyed the sky
- Why SETI watched the hydrogen line near 1420 MHz
- What the 6EQUJ5 intensity pattern meant
- Why dual feed horns and beam transit mattered
- How later observations failed to reproduce the signal
- Why the debate remains open without claiming certainty

No conspiracy claims — just the evidence, the methods, and the open questions that still drive the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

Follow for more history, mystery, and science documentaries.

snippet.title: Cuba Missile Crisis: 13 Days to Nuclear War
snippet.description:
The Cuban Missile Crisis was a 13-day confrontation between the US and USSR. The crisis began on October 16, 1962, and lasted until October 28, 1962, marking one of the most significant crises between the two superpowers during the Cold War. The Soviet Union, led by Nikita Khrushchev, sought to expand its influence in the Western Hemisphere by placing nuclear-capable ballistic missiles in Cuba, just 90 miles from the United States. This move was a direct response to the United States' deployment of Jupiter missiles in Turkey, which bordered the Soviet Union.
